routes.reason: Part II InverseGaloisPartIIHurwitzHomologicalStability under parent InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups. The title reproduces the parent's atlas title exactly and extends it ("Inverse Galois theory and arithmetic fundamental groups, Part II: homological stability of Hurwitz spaces"), the area arithmeticgeometry is a galaxy id in data/galaxies.json, and the roadmap id is free in the atlas. The mathematics is genuinely unowned: IG.3 (Branch cycles, rigidity and descent) and IG.5 (Hurwitz spaces and function-field branches) plan branch-cycle descent and arithmetic Hurwitz moduli, but nothing in the atlas plans the braid-orbit ring R, the K-complex degree estimates of §4, the truncated arc/coset resolution of §5 or the stabilization theorem itself, and a search of all 1968 stages finds no competing Hurwitz homological-stability owner. The brief states the final theorem with its actual operator U and range n>Ap+B, keeps the connected and center-free quotient variants, names what to import, and is explicit that Frobenius-equivariant stabilization and fixed-q Cohen–Lenstra convergence are not promised — which is right, since §7.9 of the paper says the equivariance is not proved. Its instruction to audit a reusable noncommutative left/right Tor interface before assigning ownership is the correct call: R is noncommutative and Mathlib's CategoryTheory.Tor is an abstract monoidal derived functor, not a graded left/right module Tor.

Source route to InverseGaloisAndArithmeticFundamentalGroups:IG.3, IG.5, IG.0, IG.1; all four stage ids resolve in data/atlas.json and their descriptions plan what is sent to them — IG.0 the Galois-category/fibre-functor dictionary, IG.1 arithmetic exact sequences and specialization, IG.3 branch cycles and descent, IG.5 Hurwitz spaces and function-field branches. The 23 items are the cover, moduli and comparison adapters, and the route keeps only the marked/unmarked and tame-family adapters locally while importing Riemann existence, curve moduli and étale/nearby-cycle foundations from their owners; the labelled polynomial-family adapter (items 126–137) is placed at IG.0/IG.1 with general quotient-stack construction left to AlgebraicModuliForArithmeticGeometry:R09.4, which is the right division.

Source route to ArithmeticStatistics:ST.0 (Families, heights and measures) and ST.5 (Beyond first moments); both stage ids resolve and both descriptions plan what is sent to them. The 46 items are the Cohen–Lenstra measure and its moment characterization, the generalized-dihedral counting dictionary, the monodromy/component computation and the large-q density theorem — exactly first- and higher-moment function-field statistics. The route imports stability, class field theory, Jacobians, trace and weights rather than claiming them, and does not assert that any of these statistical results already exist in Lean.
